##### Summary
Closes #9032 

If the agent is re-claimed at run-time then the new claim_id is not applied to the base-topic for the ACLK. This causes the broker to kick the agent for writing to the wrong topic.

##### Component Name
ACLK

##### Test Plan

* Start a claimed agent
* Remove the agent from its room
* Re-claim the agent (without stopping it), using -id=$(uuidgen)
* Re-connect the agent

##### Additional Information

Manage this branch in Squash

Test this branch here: https://amosstopic-fix-auto9.squash.io

Hmm testing it got me into infinite reconnection loop of some kind :/
Might not be related to this PR though.
I will send you logfile over slack and retest just in case it was some random failure.
It looks like the problem is caused by changing the claiming data while the link is operational. We should probably tear-down the connection if the claiming state is reloaded.
Just for the record *(as i have memory of gold fish)*, I did skip the `Remove the agent from its room` step in test plan when this happened.
Rebased - new fix is a mutex around the `claim_id` to address @stelfrag 's concern, and I've moved the topic creation earlier to fix the problem with the LWT that @hmoragrega diagnosed.
Fails in CI/CD - I need to check what is different to the build on my local system...

CI/CD picked up a real problem - we had some existing code that would have failed the build when the cloud deps were not available. This has been in master for a while but not triggered the failure before. Fixed now.

1. Remove from war room

3. Node now unreachable

Which node is unreachable - the original (which is still in the space) or the new one? How is the user telling them apart?

Just to note: did you change something about this in last night's update? I went in this morning to reproduce the test for you and suddently it appears to be working (before doing anything).  The "unclaimed / unreachable node" is now showing data.

That being said, I will go through the steps now to try and reproduce it:

1) I go to manage war room > nodes and remove the node.
2) I go into my node command line and delete the cloud.d folder (unclaim the agent) as per https://learn.netdata.cloud/docs/agent/claim/#unclaim-remove-an-agent-from-netdata-cloud
```
root@media /home/jose # cd /var/lib/netdata
root@media /var/lib/netdata # sudo rm -rf cloud.d/
```
3) I restart netdata: 
```
root@media /var/lib/netdata # service netdata restart
```
4) I go to manage a new (different) war room > nodes and click the plus sign (to add a new node) and copy the claim command (I am hiding sensitive info below)
5) I pasted the command on CLI:
```
root@media /var/lib/netdata # sudo netdata-claim.sh -token=** -rooms=** -url=https://app.netdata.cloud
Token: ****************
Base URL: https://app.netdata.cloud
Id: **
Rooms: **
Hostname: **
Proxy:

.......................................................+++++

writing RSA key
The agent cloud base url is set to the url provided.
The cloud may have different credentials already registered for this agent ID and it cannot be reclaimed under different credentials for security reasons. If you are unable to connect use -id=$(uuidgen) to overwrite this agent ID with a fresh value if the original credentials cannot be restored.
Failed to claim node with the following error message:"already claimed"
```
6) Because of the error I try again with id=$(uuidgen)
```
root@media /var/lib/netdata # sudo netdata-claim.sh -token=** -rooms=** -url=https://app.netdata.cloud -id=$(uuidgen)
Token: ****************
Base URL: https://app.netdata.cloud
Id: **
Rooms: **
Hostname: **
Proxy: 
Netdata user: **
Node was successfully claimed.
```
7) I go back to the cloud app and I can see the node there again in "unreachable" mode and no data (just like the provided screenshot from the OP).

So after re-taking the steps, it appears to be "broken" still, but it is important to clarify that when I first logged on this morning (after having left it in the same stage last night) it was working (or seemed to be working).

So I am unclear if it takes a while for the cloud app to "properly reconnect" or if it keeps trying in the background or if you issued a nightly update that affected this since last night.

The issue can still be reproduced with the steps above (at least in my environment).

Cheers,
Jose R. Lopez

Update: I forgot to mention that I also tried:

```
root@media /var/lib/netdata # netdatacli reload-claiming-state
```
But this didn't do anything towards the issue either.

@momon  Hi, we've run into a delay. The bug that we fixed has uncovered something more serious and we need to diagnose another problem before we can release this. 

While I was replicating it though I've worked out why it went wrong -
Step 5 - this sets up the claimed state of the agent and it tries to connect to the cloud.
Step 6 - at the end of the new claim it reloads the state in the agent memory.

There is an undefined state in the middle (it is the reason there is a warning message that we do not know if the claim succeeded or not) and overwriting the state with the new claiming credentials then causes a problem.

There is a very easy work-around - stop the agent, run the new claim with the random id and then restart the agent. This is probably why it started working overnight - the auto-update would have caused the agent to start and then it has a consistent claiming state.

I hope the workaround is useful - it will be a few days until we've investigated the new problem and fixed it cleanly. Edit: forgot to say - thanks for the kind words, it's great to hear.
